delea2/el cristal.why: All three examples were idioms or crystals — a glass ceiling, an obsession with crystals, 'clear as crystal' — and none was the everyday sense in Spain: glass, and above all a window pane, limpiar los cristales.

obsesionado con los cristales

delea2/guardar.why: The gloss gave the computing sense twice over and missed 'to keep, to put away', which two of the examples are. delea2/la fotografía.why: The gloss is right, and the card did not say that la foto, A1's card, is the everyday form. The first example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Esa es la fotografía de mi hermana menor.
ex: Me encanta la fotografía.

delea2/el anuncio.why: THE GLOSS MISSED THE WORD'S COMMONEST SENSE: every example was an advertisement, and the gloss gave only 'announcement, notice'. 'commercial' is American.

Read the job adverts if you're looking for work.
tu anuncio de televisión favorito

delea2/la fiebre.why: The gloss is right. The first and second examples were one construction, un poco de fiebre, twice.
dropEx: Tienes un poco de fiebre hoy
exEn: Esta mañana he tenido un poco de fiebre
I had a bit of a temperature this morning.

If the fever doesn't come down, call the doctor.

delea2/el piano.why: The gloss is right. The second example wrote como for the interrogative cómo ('aprender cómo afinar pianos'). The first is shared with tocar earlier in A2. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.

aprender como afinar pianos

delea2/cruzar.why: 'to exchange (words)' is not A2. The third example is el cruce, a crossroads, matched on shared letters, and the first is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).

dropEx: Cuidado con los coches al cruzar la calle.

está a dos metros de aquí

delea2/el vecino, la vecina.why: The gloss is a definition. The first example, a neighbour with a sword, is not a sentence a reader needs, and the third's English, 'a most gracious neighbour', is two registers above the Spanish.

delea2/montar.why: The gloss missed riding a bike (montar en bicicleta) and assembling furniture, which a reader meets at A2. delea2/la moto.why: THE GLOSS WAS WRONG: 'milestone' is not this word. la moto is a motorbike, short for la motocicleta, which is what every example says.

delea2/el metal.why: The gloss is right. The first example is shared with la madera earlier in A2. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.

delea2/la crema.why: The first example, 'toma su crema y azúcar con café', is a calque: in Spain, cream in coffee is leche, and cream from milk is la nata. The gloss's 'soup with cream' is a crema de verduras, which is worth a line.

delea2/adivinar.why: 'to divine' and 'to foretell' are not how the word is met at A2. The third example is el adivino, a fortune-teller, a noun, matched on shared letters.

delea2/enfrente.why: The gloss put 'in front of' first, which is delante de; enfrente is 'opposite', 'across the road'. She sat opposite me.

delea2/el cuadro.why: THE GLOSS MISSED THE WORD'S COMMONEST SENSE: every example was a picture or a painting, and the gloss gave only 'square, rectangle'. The first example is shared with la pared earlier in A2. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.

delea2/la bicicleta.why: The gloss ran five items together, two of them not English ('step over', 'pedalada'). The first example is shared with subir earlier in A2; the third's English said 'I bicycled'. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.

delea2/mejorar.why: The second example is la mejora, a noun, matched on shared letters, and the third wrote 'de poco a poco', where Spanish says poco a poco. ¡que te mejores!, 'get well soon', had no line.

va mejorando de poco a poco

delea2/la comisaría.why: The gloss is right. The second example, a man whose picture hangs in every police station in the country, is a line out of a film.

delea2/ocurrir.why: 'to come up with' is ocurrirse (se me ocurre), which the card did not say. The first example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).

delea2/la reserva.why: The gloss ran a booking and a nature reserve together. delea2/el dormitorio.why: The gloss is right. The first and third examples were also A1 sentences, and the second's departamento is Latin American, where Spain says piso. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).

delea2/la publicidad.why: The gloss put 'advertisement' first, which is un anuncio; la publicidad is advertising. The first example is addressed to Scott, and the second is also an A1 sentence. delea2/la barra.why: The gloss missed the two senses a reader in Spain meets daily: a loaf, una barra de pan, which is the first example, and the bar counter. The third, 'Lava tus manos', is a calque of the English possessive (lávate las manos).

delea2/las gafas.why: The third example's English said 'sunglasses' for gafas. The first is also an A1 sentence, and the second is shared with la seguridad earlier in A2. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).

delea2/la rueda.why: The gloss missed a tyre (se nos pinchó una rueda). Two of the three examples were also A1 sentences, and the first's English said 'tire'. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).

delea2/el carácter.why: The gloss gave 'character' twice. tener mal carácter, 'to be bad-tempered', which is how the word is used about people every day, had no line, and the third example is an abstract claim about the environment.

delea2/adolescente.why: The gloss gave only the adjective, 'adolescent', while both examples were the noun, a teenager, which is the A2 word. The card carried two examples where the type shows three. The first is shared with picante in B1 and stays here.
ex: Tengo dos hijos adolescentes.
I have two teenage children.

delea2/devolver.why: The gloss ran nine English verbs and an 'etc.' together, and missed taking something back to a shop. The first and third examples both returned a book.
dropEx: Devuelve el libro para mañana
exEn: Tengo que devolver el libro antes del sábado
I have to give the book back before Saturday.
ex: ¿Puedo devolver estos zapatos?
Can I take these shoes back?

delea2/el billete.why: THE GLOSS AND THE EXAMPLES DISAGREED: the gloss gave 'banknote, bill, billet' and every example was a ticket, the sense a reader needs at any station. A concert ticket is una entrada (A1), so the third example was the wrong word for its own English; the second is shared with sacar earlier in A2, and the first's English said 'round-trip'. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
senses: ticket (for a train, a bus, a plane)
forms: la entrada — ticket (for a concert, the cinema)
dropEx: Esta es la cola para sacar los billetes.
un billete para el concierto
exEn: un billete de ida y vuelta
Did you buy a return ticket?
ex: Solo tengo un billete de cincuenta euros.
I've only got a fifty-euro note.
Compré el billete de tren por internet.
I bought the train ticket online.

delea2/musical.why: The part-of-speech label read '[adjective, not músico, música]', a note to the generator that reached the card. The examples are right; the third is shared with la eléctrica later in A2 and stays here.

delea2/naranja.why: 'Pertaining to Ciudadanos' is a Spanish political party's colour and not a sense a vocabulary card should teach. The card did not say that the colour is invariable (unos zapatos naranja) or that the fruit is la naranja, which the second example is. Two examples were also A1 sentences, one with the American 'pants'. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: orange (the colour; invariable: unos zapatos naranja)
dropEx: La corona del rey es de color naranja.
pantalones de algodón de color naranja
ex: Me he comprado una camiseta naranja.
I've bought an orange T-shirt.
Un zumo de naranja, por favor.
An orange juice, please.

delea2/plástico, plástica.why: The second example is la plástica, art as a school subject, and not the material. The card did not say that el plástico is also a noun, which the first and third examples are.
dropEx: El profesor de plástica pinta por la noche.
ex: Hay que reciclar las botellas de plástico.
Plastic bottles need recycling.

delea2/la mantequilla.why: The gloss is right. The first example is also an A1 sentence, and the third is shared with el azúcar earlier in A2. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: A él le gusta el pan con mantequilla.
El azúcar es dulce, la mantequilla es grasa.
ex: ¿Me pasas la mantequilla?
Could you pass the butter?
Esta tarta lleva mucha mantequilla.
This cake has a lot of butter in it.

delea2/la hoja.why: 'petal' is not this word, and the gloss missed a sheet of paper, which two of the three examples were. The second is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: En otoño, las hojas caen de los árboles.
Esta hoja explica la filosofía
ex: Escribe tu nombre en la hoja.
Write your name on the sheet.
Los árboles ya tienen hojas nuevas.
The trees already have new leaves.

delea2/cometer.why: The gloss is right. The first example is shared with el error earlier in A2, the second's 'en igual cantidad de líneas' is stilted, and the third's English said 'I'm prisoner'. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
dropEx: Ella ha vuelto a cometer el mismo error.
en igual cantidad de líneas
exEn: Estoy preso por un crimen
I'm in prison for a crime I didn't commit.
ex: Todos cometemos errores.
We all make mistakes.
La policía no sabe quién cometió el robo.
The police don't know who committed the robbery.

delea2/la docena.why: All three examples were one sentence: a dozen eggs, bought, bought twice over, and needed.
dropEx: Ella compró dos docenas de huevos.
Ana necesita una docena de huevos.
ex: Había una docena de personas en la sala.
There were a dozen people in the room.
Te lo he dicho docenas de veces.
I've told you dozens of times.

delea2/las medias.why: 'pantyhose' is American and 'three of a kind in mus' is a card game; in Spain las medias are tights. The first example's English said 'socks', which is the Latin American sense and is what the card should warn about rather than teach; the third's said 'a run', where British English says a ladder.
forms: in much of Latin America las medias are socks (Spain: los calcetines)
dropEx: Se quitó los zapatos y las medias.
exEn: Tienes una carrera en las medias
You've got a ladder in your tights.
ex: Hace frío, ponte medias.
It's cold, put some tights on.

delea2/la novela.why: 'soap opera' is la telenovela, and is Latin American shorthand. The first example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Esta novela de ciencia ficción es muy interesante.
ex: Estoy leyendo una novela de misterio.
I'm reading a mystery novel.

delea2/la academia.why: The card did not say that in Spain una academia is above all a private school — una academia de idiomas — which is the sense a learner uses. The first example, a Kabyle academy, is not a sentence anyone needs, and the second's 'le ameritó' is Latin American.
senses: (private) school (una academia de idiomas — a language school)
dropEx: crear una academia de cabilio
le ameritó un Premio
ex: Estudio inglés en una academia.
I study English at a language school.
La Real Academia Española publica el diccionario.
The Royal Spanish Academy publishes the dictionary.

delea2/las matemáticas.why: The gloss is right. The second and third examples were one sentence reversed ('the essence of mathematics is liberty', 'the essence of liberty is mathematics'), the second also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: La esencia de las matemáticas es la libertad.
La esencia de la libertad son las matemáticas.
ex: Mañana tengo examen de matemáticas.
I've got a maths exam tomorrow.
Las matemáticas no se me dan bien.
I'm not good at maths.

delea2/la cabina.why: The gloss named a plane's and a ship's cabin while every example was a telephone box, and the first and third were one question.
dropEx: ¿En dónde puedo encontrar una cabina telefónica?
ex: El piloto está en la cabina.
The pilot is in the cockpit.

delea2/el deporte.why: The gloss did not name hacer deporte, 'to do sport'. The first example is shared with el hielo earlier in A2, and the second with libre. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
dropEx: El hockey sobre hielo es un deporte emocionante.
Él no tiene tiempo libre para hacer deportes.
ex: ¿Qué deporte practicas?
What sport do you do?
Hago deporte tres veces por semana.
I do sport three times a week.

delea2/el champán.why: The gloss read 'champan', which is not English. The card carried two examples where the type shows three, and did not say that the second's la champaña is the form used in much of Latin America.
forms: la champaña — the form in much of Latin America
ex: Brindamos con champán.
We toasted with champagne.

delea2/la agenda.why: The gloss put 'agenda' first; in Spain una agenda is above all a diary or planner, and a person's schedule. The second example, 'Siento haberte llamado fuera de tu complicada agenda', is a calque.
dropEx: fuera de tu complicada agenda
ex: Lo apunto en mi agenda.
I'll write it in my diary.

delea2/seco, seca.why: The gloss is right. The first example, 'El agua es mojado', gives water the wrong gender and is a riddle rather than a sentence; the third's English said 'fall'.
dropEx: El agua es mojado
exEn: La calle está cubierta de hojas secas
It's autumn. The street is covered in dry leaves.
ex: Tengo la boca seca.
My mouth is dry.

delea2/la corbata.why: The gloss said 'tie' twice. The first example, 'hace buen par con tu traje', is not how Spanish says it (hace juego), and the third wrote 'le queda bien a tu camisa', which is for clothes suiting a person.
dropEx: hace buen par con tu traje
La corbata le queda bien a tu camisa.
ex: Mi padre lleva corbata todos los días.
My father wears a tie every day.
¿Tengo que llevar corbata a la boda?
Do I have to wear a tie to the wedding?

delea2/la lata.why: The gloss ran six items together, 'tin-plate' among them, and missed ¡qué lata!, 'what a pain!', which is how a reader in Spain hears the word most often after the can. The third example's English said 'in opening'.
exEn: Se cortó un dedo al abrir una lata
He cut his finger opening a tin.

delea2/típico, típica.why: The gloss broke off mid-parenthesis. It did not say that típico is also 'traditional, local' — la comida típica — which is how a visitor meets it. The examples are right.

delea2/cuyo.why: The examples are right. The gloss did not say the one thing that makes the word hard: it agrees with what is owned, not with the owner, which the three examples show without saying.
senses: whose (agrees with what is owned: cuya hija, cuyos libros)

delea2/la cafetería.why: The examples were an American school canteen — a food fight, dirty public-school cafeterias — while in Spain una cafetería is a café, the gloss's own first sense.
dropEx: Hubo una pelea de comida
cafeterías en las escuelas públicas
ex: Te espero en la cafetería de la esquina.
I'll wait for you in the café on the corner.
Desayuno en una cafetería cerca del trabajo.
I have breakfast at a café near work.

delea2/la receta.why: The gloss is right. The third example's English added an exclamation mark the Spanish does not have.
exEn: Ve al doctor para que te dé una receta
Go to the doctor to get a prescription.

delea2/plano, plana.why: THE CARD TAUGHT THE WRONG WORD. It was headed as the adjective, 'plane, level, flat', while the A2 word is el plano, a street map or plan (¿tiene un plano de la ciudad?), which the second example is. The first, 'debiste haber rechazado su solicitud de plano', is not Spanish; the third was the adjective. el mapa, a map of a country, is A1's card.
senses: (street) map, plan (un plano de la ciudad)
forms: plano, plana (adjective) — flat; el mapa — map (of a country, A1)
dropEx: rechazado su solicitud de plano
cree que la Tierra es plana
ex: ¿Tiene un plano del metro?
Have you got a metro map?
Mira en el plano dónde está el museo.
Look on the map to see where the museum is.
exEn: ¿Vende planos de la ciudad
Do you sell street maps of the town, please?

delea2/escoger.why: The gloss is right. The third example, living on a star, is a fantasy rather than a sentence.
dropEx: vivir en una estrella
ex: Escoge el color que más te guste.
Choose the colour you like best.

delea2/propietario, propietaria.why: THE CARD TAUGHT THE WRONG WORD. It was headed as the adjective, 'proprietary, owning', while every example was the noun, the owner. The headword becomes the pair; the adjective goes in Forms.

delea2/generoso, generosa.why: The gloss is right. The first example, 'Él es generoso, así que vayamos con él', is not a sentence anyone says.
dropEx: así que vayamos con él
ex: Gracias, eres muy generoso.
Thank you, you're very generous.

delea2/actualmente.why: The gloss is right and the card owed its reader a warning: actualmente is a false friend of 'actually', which is en realidad. The first example used the Latin American auto.
dropEx: su padre va a trabajar en auto
ex: Actualmente vivo en Barcelona.
I currently live in Barcelona.

delea2/la exposición.why: THE GLOSS MISSED THE WORD'S COMMONEST SENSE: every example was an exhibition, and the gloss gave only 'exposition, exposure'. The third example, applying to be an attendant at an exhibition, is stilted.
dropEx: Eché una solicitud como empleado
exEn: las exposiciones en Rumanía
Did you enjoy going to the exhibitions in Romania?
ex: Fuimos a ver una exposición de Picasso.
We went to see a Picasso exhibition.

delea2/la región.why: The gloss is right. The third example wrote video, where Spain says vídeo, and is a message on a screen rather than a sentence.
dropEx: Este video no está disponible
ex: Galicia es una región muy verde.
Galicia is a very green region.

delea2/el dibujo.why: 'tread' is a tyre's, and not A2. The first example, 'Ana tiene muchos dibujos que hacer', is stilted, and the second is shared with el/la artista earlier in A2. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
dropEx: Ana tiene muchos dibujos que hacer.
El dibujo del artista fue hecho en carbón.
ex: Mi hijo hace dibujos de animales.
My son draws animals.
Me encanta este dibujo.
I love this drawing.

delea2/apagar.why: THE GLOSS MISSED THE SENSE EVERY EXAMPLE USED: 'to extinguish, to douse, to slake (thirst' broke off mid-parenthesis and never said 'to turn off', which is all three examples. The first two were one sentence, turning off a light.
senses: to turn off, to switch off
to put out (a fire, a cigarette)
dropEx: Que no se te olvide apagar la luz.
ex: Apagaron el fuego en una hora.
They put the fire out in an hour.

delea2/pintar.why: The gloss said 'to paint' twice. The third example, 'Las mujeres a menudo se pintan las uñas', is a generalisation.
dropEx: Las mujeres a menudo se pintan las uñas.
ex: Mi hija pinta muy bien.
My daughter paints very well.

delea2/la eléctrica.why: EVERY EXAMPLE WAS ANOTHER WORD: the adjective eléctrico, which is B2's card, three times — two electric guitars and some power tools. la eléctrica is the electricity company, as the gloss says, and now has examples that are it. The first example was also an A1 sentence and the third is shared with musical earlier in A2. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Mi hermano se ha comprado una guitarra eléctrica.
herramientas eléctricas
Mi instrumento musical favorito
ex: La eléctrica me ha subido la factura.
The electricity company has put my bill up.
Llamé a la eléctrica porque no había luz.
I rang the electricity company because there was no power.
Las eléctricas han ganado mucho dinero este año.
The electricity companies have made a lot of money this year.

delea2/pasear.why: The gloss ran five English verbs together ('to saunter, to promenade') and did not name dar un paseo. The second example is the noun el paseo and is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: to go for a walk, to walk
dar un paseo — to go for a walk
dropEx: Mi papá da un paseo todos los días.
ex: Los domingos paseamos por el parque.
On Sundays we go for a walk in the park.

delea2/generalmente.why: All three examples were also A1 sentences. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Las mujeres generalmente viven más
Generalmente me voy a casa a las cuatro.
tomo un baño en la noche
ex: Generalmente voy al trabajo en autobús.
I generally go to work by bus.
En agosto hace generalmente mucho calor.
It's generally very hot in August.
Los niños generalmente se acuestan pronto.
Children generally go to bed early.

delea2/la poesía.why: Two of the three examples were aphorisms ('la poesía inmortal del corazón', 'el amor es la poesía de los sentidos'); the second's English said 'poetry' for poesías, poems.
dropEx: la poesía inmortal del corazón
El amor es la poesía de los sentidos.
exEn: En mi tiempo libre escribo poesías
In my free time I write poems.
ex: En el colegio aprendimos una poesía de memoria.
At school we learnt a poem by heart.
A mi abuelo le gusta mucho la poesía.
My grandfather really likes poetry.

delea2/encender.why: The gloss ran 'power up' in with 'ignite'. The third example is shared with la luz earlier in A2. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
senses: to turn on, to switch on
dropEx: Enciende las luces, si no, no puedo trabajar.
ex: ¿Puedes encender la calefacción?
Can you turn the heating on?

delea2/la colonia.why: The gloss missed cologne, which is the third example and the sense a reader in a Spanish shop meets. The second example's English said 'the English people'.
exEn: Los ingleses establecieron colonias
The English established colonies in America.

delea2/la nube.why: 'multitude, or crowd (of people)' is a figurative sense, and the third example, 'Eres una nube que cubre tu propio sol', is an aphorism.
dropEx: Eres una nube que cubre tu propio sol.
ex: Hoy hay muchas nubes.
It's very cloudy today.

delea2/la toalla.why: The gloss is right. The second example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: No hay toallas en la habitación número quince.
ex: No te olvides la toalla de playa.
Don't forget your beach towel.

delea2/reunirse.why: The gerund read reuníendose, S3's fault; it is reuniéndose. Its imperatives, reúnete and reúnase, are right. The third example met Ben, which is not a Spanish name.
dropEx: Me reuní con Ben ayer
ex: Nos reunimos todos los viernes para cenar.
We get together every Friday for dinner.

delea2/la pensión.why: The gloss is right. The second example, a government turning a blind eye to pensions, is political; the third's English said 'hostel' where the word is a guesthouse.
dropEx: haciendo la vista gorda
exEn: Hay una pensión a dos kilómetros
There's a guesthouse two kilometres from the station.
ex: Mi abuela cobra una pensión pequeña.
My grandmother gets a small pension.

delea2/la estatua.why: The first and third examples were both the Statue of Liberty.
dropEx: Esta es la Estatua de la Libertad.
ex: En la plaza hay una estatua de Cervantes.
There's a statue of Cervantes in the square.

delea2/el maletín.why: The gloss is right, and two of the three examples' English said 'suitcase', which is la maleta — the confusion the card most needs to prevent.
exEn: Dejaré los maletines
I'll put the briefcases in Carlos's room.
cómo abrir este maletín
I can't work out how to open this briefcase.

delea2/la mochila.why: 'backpack' is American. The second example, 'La mochila pesa por los libros de física', is not how Spanish says it; the third's English said 'bag'.
dropEx: La mochila pesa por los libros de física.
exEn: Se me olvidó mi mochila
I left my rucksack somewhere.
Ella puso la llave en su mochila
She put the key in her rucksack.
ex: Mete el bocadillo en la mochila.
Put the sandwich in the rucksack.

delea2/los correos.why: The card was headed los correos, a plural nobody uses for this: the post office in Spain is Correos, the name of the postal service, with a capital. The first example is also an A1 sentence, and the third's 'fue derecho' is Latin American. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: the post office (the Spanish postal service)
la oficina de correos — the post office
dropEx: ¿Hay un buzón de correos cerca de aquí?
fue derecho a la oficina de correos
ex: Tengo que ir a Correos a enviar un paquete.
I have to go to the post office to send a parcel.
Correos abre a las nueve.
The post office opens at nine.

delea2/las urgencias.why: 'emergency room' and 'ER' are American; the British is A&E. The examples are right.
exEn: le tuve que llevar a urgencias
He'd fallen, so I had to take him to A&E.
Tuve que ir a urgencias
I had to go to A&E.
Se encuentra en urgencias
He's in A&E.

delea2/el pañuelo.why: The gloss missed the tissue, pañuelo de papel, which is the sense a reader uses most. The first and third examples were one sentence, a headscarf taken off and put on.
dropEx: Ella tenía puesto un pañuelo de cabeza.
ex: ¿Tienes un pañuelo de papel?
Have you got a tissue?

delea2/durar.why: The third example is the adjective duro, 'hard', matched on shared letters; it is B1's card. The second's English said 'remains'.
dropEx: El hierro es más duro que el oro.
exEn: nada dura para siempre
After all, nothing lasts for ever.
ex: La película dura dos horas.
The film lasts two hours.

delea2/la niebla.why: The gloss said 'fog' twice. The second example, 'Londres ya no es más una ciudad de nieblas', is a calque of 'no longer', where Spanish says ya no es.
dropEx: Londres ya no es más una ciudad de nieblas.
ex: Por la mañana hay niebla en el valle.
There's fog in the valley in the morning.

delea2/invitar.why: 'to be on' was a garbled 'it's on me': invitar is also to treat someone, te invito, which is how a reader in Spain hears it at every bar and had no line of its own. The second example is the noun los invitados and is shared with recibir earlier in A2. The third is shared with alegrarse later in A2 and stays here. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
senses: to treat, to pay for (te invito — it's on me)
dropEx: Estamos a punto de recibir a los invitados.
ex: Hoy te invito yo.
It's on me today.

delea2/la talla.why: The gloss said 'size' twice. The examples are right.

delea2/la bañera.why: 'cockpit' is not this word. The second example, 'Los niños mueren a menudo en la bañera', is a statement about children dying, and the first is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Los niños mueren a menudo en la bañera.
Deja correr el agua caliente por la bañera.
exEn: le gusta cantar en la bañera
He likes to sing in the bath.
ex: Me gusta relajarme en la bañera.
I like to relax in the bath.
Nuestro baño tiene ducha pero no bañera.
Our bathroom has a shower but no bath.

delea2/el pop.why: The word has no plural in use and the card gave one; the first and second examples were one sentence, Russian pop.
dropEx: A ella le gusta el pop ruso.
ex: Escucho sobre todo música pop.
I mostly listen to pop music.

delea2/certificado, certificada.why: The gloss gave only 'certified', while two of the examples were the noun, a certificate, and the adjective is met at A2 as una carta certificada, 'registered letter', which the gloss did not name. The third example, the paperwork for a passport, is not A2.
dropEx: ¿Qué certificados y trámites hacen falta
ex: Necesito un certificado médico para el trabajo.
I need a doctor's certificate for work.

delea2/el menú.why: The plural was given as 'menúes'; the standard plural is menús. The gloss said 'menu' twice and missed el menú del día, the set lunch every Spanish restaurant offers.
senses: el menú del día — the set menu
dropEx: déjame echar una mirada al menú
ex: El menú del día cuesta doce euros.
The set menu costs twelve euros.

delea2/la ópera.why: The gloss is right. The first example is also an A1 sentence, with ruta for a bus route; the third wrote 'en frente', which is enfrente. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: La ruta 12 para cerca
en frente de la ópera
ex: Nunca he ido a la ópera.
I've never been to the opera.
La ópera empieza a las ocho.
The opera starts at eight.

delea2/nacer.why: 'to sprout', 'to grow' and 'to rise' are figurative senses nobody at A2 needs. The second and third examples were one construction, the place where someone was born.
dropEx: Ésta es la ciudad en la que nací.
ex: ¿En qué año naciste?
What year were you born?

delea2/girar.why: The gloss ran seven English verbs together. The third example is el Giro de Italia, a race, matched on shared letters.
dropEx: Carlos ganó el Giro de Italia.
ex: Gira la llave dos veces.
Turn the key twice.

delea2/moderno, moderna.why: The gloss is right. The first two examples are shared with el arte and la tecnología earlier in A2. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
dropEx: A Carlos no le gusta el arte moderno.
La tecnología moderna nos da muchas cosas nuevas.
ex: Vive en un piso muy moderno.
He lives in a very modern flat.
Mi abuela es muy moderna.
My grandmother is very modern.

delea2/el ajedrez.why: The gloss is right; the word has no plural in use. The third example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Te voy a enseñar a jugar al ajedrez.
ex: ¿Jugamos una partida de ajedrez?
Shall we have a game of chess?

delea2/el cordero, la cordera.why: The gloss is right. Two of the three examples were the same proverb (a wolf in sheep's clothing), both kept by earlier A2 cards, la piel and político; the lamb a reader eats had no example. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
dropEx: Él es un lobo con piel de cordero.
Algunos políticos son lobos con piel de cordero.
exEn: Los corderos estaban haciendo mucho ruido
The lambs were making a lot of noise.
ex: Hemos comido cordero asado.
We had roast lamb.
En primavera nacen los corderos.
Lambs are born in spring.

delea2/la matrícula.why: The gloss put 'matriculation' first; at A2 the word is a car's number plate and enrolment on a course. The second example used the Latin American auto, and the third, a traffic restriction on even number plates, is not A2 and said 'license plates'.
senses: number plate, registration number (of a car)
dropEx: la matrícula del auto
vehículos con matrícula par
ex: Anoté la matrícula del coche.
I wrote down the car's number plate.
El plazo de matrícula termina el viernes.
Enrolment closes on Friday.

delea2/el cocinero, la cocinera.why: The gloss is right. The first example is shared with diferente earlier in A2, and the third, 'Los griegos son buenos cocineros', is a generalisation about a nation. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
dropEx: El cocinero prepara platos diferentes
Los griegos son buenos cocineros.
ex: Mi padre es cocinero en un restaurante.
My father is a cook in a restaurant.
Soy muy mal cocinero.
I'm a terrible cook.

delea2/el jazz.why: The gloss is right. The first and third examples were one construction, liking or not liking jazz.
dropEx: A Carlos no le gusta el jazz.
ex: Esta noche hay un concierto de jazz.
There's a jazz concert tonight.

delea2/aéreo, aérea.why: 'aerial' is not how the word is met: it is 'air' as an adjective, in correo aéreo and línea aérea, which are the examples. The second example was a fragment.
senses: air (correo aéreo — airmail; compañía aérea — airline)
dropEx: A la oficina de la línea aérea.
ex: Compramos los billetes en una compañía aérea de bajo coste.
We bought the tickets from a low-cost airline.

delea2/las afueras.why: The gloss is right. The second and third examples were one sentence, and the third's English said 'the skirts of the city'.
dropEx: Su casa está a las afueras de la ciudad.
ex: En las afueras hay un centro comercial enorme.
There's a huge shopping centre on the outskirts.

delea2/el ayuntamiento.why: The gloss ran five items together, and all three examples' English said 'city hall', which is American.
exEn: La oficina del alcalde está en el ayuntamiento
The mayor's office is in the town hall.
tiene mucha influencia en el ayuntamiento
My father has a lot of influence at the town hall.
de la estación al ayuntamiento
Do you know how far it is from the station to the town hall?

delea2/la factura.why: 'quality' and 'caliber' are not this word. The first example, '¿Cómo hacer un pago de factura en línea?', is a calque of an English search query.
dropEx: un pago de factura en línea
ex: La factura de la luz ha subido mucho.
The electricity bill has gone up a lot.

delea2/la tapa.why: The gloss missed the tapa, the small dish served in a Spanish bar, which is the second example and the sense every visitor meets; its English said 'small and large portions'. 'the bottom of a shoe's heel' is a cobbler's word.
senses: tapa (a small dish served in a bar)
exEn: Tenemos tapas y raciones
We have tapas and larger portions.

delea2/despedirse.why: The gloss is right; the gerund read despidíendose, S3's fault, and is now despidiéndose. The second example's English said 'tell Ana goodbye'.
exEn: no tuvo la oportunidad de despedirse de Ana
Carlos didn't get a chance to say goodbye to Ana.

delea2/reservado, reservada.why: The first example is the verb reservar, 'He reservado una mesa', which is its own card later in A2. The gloss did not separate a booked seat from a reserved person, and the third example's English said 'secretive'.
dropEx: He reservado una mesa para cuatro personas.
exEn: Ella fue siempre muy reservada
She was always very reserved.
ex: Esta mesa está reservada.
This table is reserved.

delea2/mecánico, mecánica.why: The gloss gave only the adjective, while the first example was the noun, a mechanic, which is the sense a car owner needs. The second and third examples were one construction, the escalator.
dropEx: La escalera mecánica se detuvo de repente.
ex: Tengo que llevar el coche al mecánico.
I have to take the car to the mechanic.

delea2/la gripe.why: NONE OF THE THREE EXAMPLES COULD STAY. The first used the Latin American agarrarse for coger; the second spelt the word gripa, which is Latin American, and translated it as 'a cold'; the third caught 'summer flu' in spring.
dropEx: se agarró la gripe
algo para la gripa
cogí una gripe de verano
ex: Estoy en la cama con gripe.
I'm in bed with flu.
Este invierno ha habido mucha gripe.
There's been a lot of flu this winter.
Me he vacunado contra la gripe.
I've had the flu jab.

delea2/postal.why: The gloss gave only the adjective, while every example was the noun, la postal, a postcard, and código postal, the postcode, had no line. The first and third examples were one sentence, a postcard to Japan.
dropEx: Me gustaría enviar esta postal a Japón.
ex: ¿Cuál es tu código postal?
What's your postcode?

delea2/portátil.why: The gloss gave only 'portable', while two of the examples were the noun, el portátil, a laptop, which is the A2 word in Spain. The second used the Latin American computadoras; the third, a laptop in the bath, is not a sentence anyone needs.
dropEx: nuestras computadoras portátiles
mi portátil en la bañera
ex: Me he comprado un portátil nuevo.
I've bought a new laptop.
Llevamos una radio portátil a la playa.
We took a portable radio to the beach.

delea2/ordenar.why: The gloss put 'to order' first and missed 'to tidy', which is the first example and the everyday sense. It also did not warn that ordering food is pedir in Spain.
senses: to tidy (up), to put in order
forms: to order (food, in a restaurant) — pedir
exEn: es un rollo ordenar la habitación
It's a pain tidying the room, though.
me ordenó estar aquí
Carlos told me to be here at 2:30 tomorrow.

delea2/la gorra.why: The second example's 'gorras de lana' are woolly hats, which in Spain are gorros (B1's card), and the third was worn by Sami.
dropEx: gorras de lana en invierno
Sami llevaba puesta
ex: Ponte la gorra, hace mucho sol.
Put your cap on, it's very sunny.
Mi hijo colecciona gorras de béisbol.
My son collects baseball caps.

delea2/el tomate.why: The gloss said 'tomato' twice. The first example, a poem about a tomato, teaches nothing; the third's English said 'can'.
dropEx: un poema sobre un tomate
exEn: esa lata de tomate
I can't reach that tin of tomatoes.
ex: Una ensalada de tomate, por favor.
A tomato salad, please.

delea2/la mosca.why: 'fly (boxing class)' is not A2. The first and third examples were one idiom, not harming a fly, and the first used the Latin American lastimar.
dropEx: no puede lastimar ni a una mosca
exEn: incapaz de hacer daño a una mosca
He looks as if he couldn't hurt a fly.
ex: Hay una mosca en mi sopa.
There's a fly in my soup.

delea2/el jamón.why: The gloss is right. The second example, 'Los cerdos de hoy son los jamones de mañana', is not a sentence anyone says, and the third put jamón in a sándwich, where Spain has un bocadillo.
dropEx: Los cerdos de hoy
Un sándwich sin jamón
ex: El jamón serrano es típico de España.
Serrano ham is typical of Spain.
Compré cien gramos de jamón.
I bought a hundred grams of ham.

delea2/la tela.why: The gloss was a definition. The examples are right.

delea2/encantar.why: The gloss gave 'to charm, to enchant', which is what the word meant once; at A2 it is me encanta, 'I love it', built like gustar, which is every example. The second example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: to love (me encanta — I love it; built like gustar)
dropEx: El color que me encanta es el rojo.
ex: Me encanta viajar.
I love travelling.

delea2/la ginebra.why: EVERY EXAMPLE WAS ANOTHER WORD: Ginebra, the city of Geneva, three times — a treaty, a man who comes from there, and its conferences. The card is gin.
dropEx: el tratado de Ginebra
Viene de Ginebra.
han tenido lugar en Ginebra
ex: No me gusta la ginebra.
I don't like gin.
Un gin-tonic lleva ginebra y tónica.
A gin and tonic is made with gin and tonic water.
¿Me pones una ginebra con limón?
Could I have a gin with lemon?

delea2/músico, música.why: THE CARD TAUGHT THE WRONG WORD. It was headed as an adjective with a note to the generator in its label ('[adjective, not musical]'), and glossed 'musical'. The A2 word is the noun, a musician. The second example was la música, 'music', which is A1's card, and that sentence is also an A1 sentence; the first is shared with científico earlier in A2. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Él es científico a la vez que músico.
A todo el mundo le gusta la música.
exEn: viene de una familia de músicos
Carlos comes from a family of musicians.
ex: Mi hermano es músico en una orquesta.
My brother is a musician in an orchestra.
Es una música muy conocida.
She's a very well-known musician.

delea2/la nevera.why: 'refrigerator' is a register above the word. The first example, 'más fea que una nevera por detrás', is an insult about a named woman, and the second, a raffle of two fridges, is not a sentence anyone needs.
dropEx: más fea que una nevera
Sorteamos un viaje a Bali
ex: Guarda la comida en la nevera.
Put the food in the fridge.
Se ha estropeado la nevera.
The fridge has broken down.

delea2/electrónico, electrónica.why: The gloss did not name correo electrónico, 'email', which two of the examples were, or the noun la electrónica, which the third was. The first is also an A1 sentence, and the second's English wrote 'e-mails'. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Carlos no revisa su correo electrónico
exEn: envió esos correos electrónicos
She sent those emails an hour ago.
ex: Me han regalado un libro electrónico.
I've been given an e-book.

delea2/la literatura.why: The gloss is right. Two of the three examples were aphorisms — 'the soul of literature', 'the future of a nation' — and the third is little more.
dropEx: El lenguaje es el alma de la literatura.
La literatura es el futuro de una nación.
ex: Estudio literatura inglesa en la universidad.
I study English literature at university.
Mi profesora de literatura es muy buena.
My literature teacher is very good.

delea2/completar.why: The gloss is right. The second and third examples were the adjective completo — 'un completo y total sin sentido', which is not Spanish, and 'la historia completa', which is also an A1 sentence; the adjective is B1's card. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: to complete, to fill in (a form)
dropEx: un completo y total sin sentido
la historia completa
ex: Completa el formulario con tus datos.
Fill in the form with your details.
Ya he completado el curso.
I've already completed the course.

delea2/el cepillo.why: 'plane (tool for smoothing wood)' is a carpenter's word, and the first example was one. The third is shared with la madera earlier in A2. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
dropEx: Los cepillos de carpintero son caros.
Mi cepillo de pelo está hecho de madera.
ex: Me he dejado el cepillo en el hotel.
I've left my hairbrush at the hotel.
Usa un cepillo para limpiar los zapatos.
Use a brush to clean your shoes.

delea2/vestirse.why: The gloss is right. The gerund read vistíendose, S3's reflexive-gerund fault, and is now vistiéndose; the vosotros imperative read vestios and is now vestíos (S2's -ir imperative finding). The second example was the noun el vestido, 'dress', not the verb.
dropEx: le gustan los vestidos azules
exEn: cuando se viste de blanco
She looks attractive when she dresses in white.
ex: Me visto y bajo a desayunar.
I get dressed and go down for breakfast.

delea2/el pintor, la pintora.why: The gloss is right, though 'housepainter' is 'decorator' in British English. The first example, 'the photographer is a kind of painter', is an aphorism.
dropEx: El fotógrafo es una especie de pintor.
ex: Picasso fue un pintor español.
Picasso was a Spanish painter.

delea2/automático, automática.why: The gloss is right. The first and third examples were one construction, the cash machine, and cajero automático had no line.
dropEx: Mucha gente usa cajeros automáticos
ex: La puerta se abre de forma automática.
The door opens automatically.

delea2/el carnicero, la carnicera.why: 'carnivoran' is a zoologist's word. The first and third examples were one construction, 'Carlos es carnicero', and the first used the article a profession does not take after ser.
dropEx: Yo sé que Carlos es un carnicero.
ex: La carnicera del mercado es muy simpática.
The butcher at the market is very friendly.

delea2/doler.why: The gloss did not say that doler is built like gustar, which is how every A2 learner meets it. The second example is also an A1 sentence, and the third was the noun el duelo, 'grief', not the verb. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: to hurt, to ache (me duele la espalda — my back hurts; built like gustar)
dropEx: Me duele el estómago después de las comidas.
No existe una forma correcta de vivir el duelo.
ex: Me duele mucho la espalda.
My back really hurts.
¿Te duelen los pies?
Do your feet hurt?

delea2/separarse.why: The gloss missed the everyday sense, a couple splitting up. The first example, 'Irlanda e Inglaterra son separados por el mar', is not reflexive and gets the agreement wrong; the third's 'se separan en dos escuelas' is not natural Spanish. The second's English said 'didn't like'.
dropEx: Irlanda e Inglaterra son separados
Los científicos se separan en dos escuelas.
exEn: no quería separarse de su familia
He didn't want to be separated from his family.
ex: Mis padres se separaron cuando yo tenía diez años.
My parents split up when I was ten.
No te separes del grupo.
Don't get separated from the group.

delea2/prestar.why: The gloss had fallen apart ('pay (e.g. • attention)'), and did not give pedir prestado, 'to borrow', which the third example is. The first example, prestar declaración, is legal language.
dropEx: se niega a prestar declaración
ex: ¿Me prestas tu bolígrafo?
Can you lend me your pen?

delea2/la margarita.why: 'pearl' is an obsolete sense. The third example, plucking a daisy for someone, is not a sentence anyone needs.
dropEx: Yo deshojé una margarita para ella.
ex: En primavera el campo se llena de margaritas.
In spring the fields fill with daisies.

delea2/el violín.why: The gloss is right. The third example is also an A1 sentence, and its English said 'would have to practice'. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Deberías practicar con el violín todos los días.
ex: Mi hermana toca el violín en una orquesta.
My sister plays the violin in an orchestra.

delea2/navegar.why: The gloss missed surfing the internet, which is the second example and what most people now mean by it.
senses: to surf, to browse (navegar por internet)

delea2/zoológico, zoológica.why: The gloss gave only the adjective, while two of the examples were the noun, el zoológico, the zoo. The second, animals from Earth in the zoos of Mars, is not a sentence anyone needs.
dropEx: En los jardines zoológicos de Marte
ex: En el zoológico hay dos elefantes.
There are two elephants at the zoo.

delea2/el alumno, la alumna.why: The gloss is right. The first example is also an A1 sentence, and the third's English said 'disrespected'. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: En nuestra clase hay cuarenta y un alumnos.
exEn: La alumna fue irrespetuosa
The pupil was rude to the teacher.
ex: Los alumnos tienen un examen mañana.
The pupils have an exam tomorrow.

delea2/el zumo.why: 'extract' and 'herbal tincture' are not this word. The examples are right.

delea2/industrial.why: The gloss is right. The first and third examples were one construction, the Industrial Revolution.
dropEx: La Revolución Industrial cambió dónde y cómo vivía la gente.
ex: Mi padre trabaja en un polígono industrial.
My father works on an industrial estate.

delea2/odiar.why: The gloss is right. The first example is shared with propio earlier in A2, and the second was the noun el odio, 'hatred', not the verb. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
dropEx: Él odiaba a los de su propia especie.
Dile no al odio
ex: Odio levantarme temprano.
I hate getting up early.
Mis hermanos se odiaban de pequeños.
My brothers hated each other when they were little.

delea2/el arquitecto, la arquitecta.why: The gloss is right. The first example, 'Es un arquitecto el que ocupa esa oficina', is not natural Spanish, and the second mixed tenses, decía que quiere.
dropEx: Es un arquitecto el que ocupa esa oficina.
Ana decía que quiere ser arquitecta.
ex: El arquitecto diseñó un edificio muy moderno.
The architect designed a very modern building.
Ana dice que quiere ser arquitecta.
Ana says she wants to be an architect.

delea2/la excursión.why: The gloss did not give ir de excursión, which the first example is. That example's English said 'we will go' for vayamos, 'let's go'.
senses: ir de excursión — to go on a trip, to go on an outing
exEn: vayamos de excursión
If the weather's good tomorrow, let's go on a trip.

delea2/el filete.why: 'thread of a screw' is an engineer's word. The third example's 'para la cena' is a calque of 'for dinner'.
dropEx: comiste filete para la cena
ex: Pedí un filete con patatas.
I ordered a steak and chips.

delea2/la gimnasia.why: The card had only two examples, and the gloss missed PE at school, which is where most learners meet the word.
ex: En el colegio tenemos gimnasia dos veces por semana.
At school we have PE twice a week.

delea2/dibujar.why: 'to describe vividly' and 'to detail' are not A2. The second example, 'Dejad que el té dibuje durante diez minutos', is a machine translation of English 'let the tea draw' and is not Spanish.
dropEx: Dejad que el té dibuje
ex: Mi hijo dibuja muy bien.
My son draws very well.

delea2/calvo, calva.why: 'bare (lacking vegetation)' is not A2. The second example was the noun la calva, 'bald patch', not the adjective.
dropEx: La calva de Carlos es brillante.
ex: Un hombre calvo me preguntó la hora.
A bald man asked me the time.

delea2/el paraguas.why: The card had only one example. The gloss is right.
ex: No olvides el paraguas, que va a llover.
Don't forget your umbrella, it's going to rain.
Me he dejado el paraguas en el autobús.
I've left my umbrella on the bus.

delea2/el kilo.why: 'the letter K in the Spanish spelling alphabet' is a radio operator's word. The third example spelt it quilo, a variant, and wrote '3€'. The second's English said 'a quarter kilogram'.
dropEx: Los kiwis salen a 3 euros
exEn: Dame un cuarto de kilo de costillas
Give me a quarter of a kilo of ribs.
ex: Un kilo de naranjas, por favor.
A kilo of oranges, please.

delea2/optimista.why: 'bullish' is a trader's word, and the gloss missed the noun, an optimist. The first example's 'como Ana es' is a calque, and the second wrote aun for aún.
dropEx: no es tan optimista como Ana es
aun son optimistas
ex: Carlos no es tan optimista como Ana.
Carlos isn't as optimistic as Ana.
Mis padres son muy optimistas.
My parents are very optimistic.

delea2/mexicano, mexicana.why: 'Mexican (pertaining to the Mexican language, i.e. Nahuatl)' is not this word at A2, and the gloss missed the noun. The second example spelt it mejicano, a variant, and its English dropped the word altogether ('a sombrero').
dropEx: lleva puesto un sombrero mejicano
ex: Mi mejor amiga es mexicana.
My best friend is Mexican.

delea2/valer.why: The gloss missed ¿cuánto vale?, 'how much is it?', the sense a shopper needs, and valer la pena. The first example, 'No todos los libros valen la pena leer', is not grammatical.
senses: to cost, to be worth (¿cuánto vale? — how much is it?)
to be good (for), to be valid
valer la pena — to be worth it
dropEx: No todos los libros valen la pena leer.
ex: ¿Cuánto vale esta camiseta?
How much is this T-shirt?

delea2/aprobar.why: The gloss put 'to approve, to condone' first; at A2 the word is passing an exam, which every example was. All three were that one construction.
dropEx: Estoy seguro de que aprobará el próximo examen.
ex: El Parlamento aprobó la nueva ley.
Parliament passed the new law.

delea2/afeitarse.why: The gloss and the examples are right. The affirmative imperatives read afeítate, afeítese, afeítense, the add_stress fault S6 found: the stress falls on the e of the diphthong, aféitate.

delea2/consultar.why: The gloss missed looking something up, the everyday sense. The first example was the noun la consulta, the surgery hours, not the verb.
senses: to look up (in a dictionary, a timetable)
dropEx: tiene el doctor la consulta
ex: Consulta el diccionario si no sabes una palabra.
Look it up in the dictionary if you don't know a word.

delea2/preocuparse.why: The gloss is right. The second and third examples were one construction, 'no te preocupes' and 'no se preocupe'.
dropEx: No se preocupe. Es un error muy común.
ex: Mi madre se preocupa mucho por mí.
My mother worries about me a lot.

delea2/enfadarse.why: The gloss did not give enfadarse con, which the second and third examples are. The first's English said 'turned away in anger', the third's 'gets mad'.
senses: to get angry, to get cross (enfadarse con — with)
exEn: Ella se enfadó y se dio la vuelta
She got angry and turned away.
se enfada conmigo por cada pequeña cosa
He gets cross with me over every little thing.

delea2/acordarse.why: The gloss did not give acordarse de. The first example is also an A1 sentence, and the third, 'Tú no te acuerdas, yo no me olvidaré', is shared with olvidar earlier in A2. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1). SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
dropEx: No me acuerdo de la cara de Carlos.
Tú no te acuerdas, yo no me olvidaré.
ex: ¿Te acuerdas de mí?
Do you remember me?
Carlos se acordó de su cumpleaños.
Carlos remembered her birthday.

delea2/repasar.why: 'to review' is American for revising; in British English a student revises, which the examples already said. The first's English read 'his exam of tomorrow'.
senses: to revise (for an exam), to go over
exEn: está repasando para su examen
Carlos is revising for tomorrow's exam.
Repasé el presupuesto
I went over the budget and decided to cut costs.

delea2/reservar.why: The gloss did not give 'to book', the British word the examples want, and listed 'keep, save, set aside' separately. The first and third examples' English said 'reservations' and 'reserve'.
senses: to book, to reserve (a table, a room)
exEn: Es imposible comer en este restaurante sin reservar
You can't eat at this restaurant without booking.
Reservaste una habitación
Did you book a room at the hotel?

delea2/divertirse.why: The gloss and the examples are right. The gerund read divirtíendose (S3's fault) and is now divirtiéndose; the vosotros imperative read divertios and is now divertíos (S2's finding).

delea2/regalar.why: 'to regale' and 'entertain' are not what the word means in Spanish today. The examples are right.

delea2/suspender.why: The gloss put 'to suspend' first; at A2 it is failing an exam, which two examples are, and 'to call off', which the first is. The third used entonces for 'so', which is Latin American; Spain says así que.
dropEx: entonces suspendió
ex: Si no estudias, vas a suspender.
If you don't study, you're going to fail.

delea2/traducir.why: The gloss said 'to translate' twice. The second example's English, 'How long have we been translating', is not what 'nos ha llevado' says, and the third's said 'Father'.
exEn: nos ha llevado traducir este libro
How long has it taken us to translate this book?
Mi padre tradujo el documento
My father translated the French document into Japanese.

delea2/barrer.why: The gloss is right. The first example was the noun el barro, 'mud', not the verb, and the third used el piso for the floor, which in Spain is a flat.
dropEx: Mi camión se quedó atascado en el barro.
que barriera el piso
ex: Barro la terraza todos los sábados.
I sweep the terrace every Saturday.
Carlos le pidió a Ana que barriera la cocina.
Carlos asked Ana to sweep the kitchen.

delea2/divorciarse.why: The gloss is right. The affirmative imperatives read divorcíate, divorcíese, divorcíense, the add_stress fault: the i of divorcio is unstressed, so it is divórciate. The first and second examples were one construction, a divorce last year.
dropEx: Carlos y Ana se divorciaron el año pasado.
ex: ¿Por qué quieren divorciarse?
Why do they want to get divorced?

delea2/interesar.why: The gloss did not say that interesar is built like gustar, which is how every example uses it. The examples are right.
senses: to interest (me interesa — I'm interested in it; built like gustar)

delea2/felicitar.why: The gloss is right. The first example, congratulating 'the hands that made this possible', is not a sentence anyone needs.
dropEx: Felicito a las manos
ex: Te felicito por el nuevo trabajo.
Congratulations on the new job.

delea2/anteayer.why: The first and third examples were one construction, a weekday riddle, and their English said 'after tomorrow'. The second spelt the word antier, which is Latin American.
dropEx: Antier terminé
Si anteayer fue miércoles
exEn: Si anteayer fue domingo
If the day before yesterday was Sunday, the day after tomorrow will be Thursday.
ex: Anteayer fuimos al cine.
The day before yesterday we went to the cinema.
Llegó anteayer de Londres.
He got back from London the day before yesterday.

delea2/quejarse.why: The gloss did not give quejarse de. The first example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: La gente se queja a menudo del tiempo.
ex: Los vecinos se quejan del ruido.
The neighbours complain about the noise.

delea2/planchar.why: 'to overwrite' is not this word. The examples are right.

delea2/memorizar.why: The gloss was spelt American; the examples already said 'memorise'.
senses: to memorise, to learn by heart

delea2/alegrarse.why: The gloss did not give alegrarse de. The first example is shared with invitar earlier in A2. SHARED WITHIN A2: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
senses: to be glad, to be pleased (alegrarse de)
dropEx: Me alegro de que Carlos te haya invitado.
ex: Me alegro de verte.
I'm glad to see you.

delea2/aburrirse.why: The gloss is right. The gerund read aburríendose (S3's fault) and the vosotros imperative aburrios (S2's); they are now aburriéndose and aburríos. The second example was sexual, and the third's 'Entre más… más' is Latin American; Spain says cuanto más.
dropEx: mientras hacíamos el amor
Entre más hablaba ella
ex: Cuanto más hablaba, más me aburría.
The more he talked, the more bored I got.
Los niños se aburren en los viajes largos.
Children get bored on long journeys.

delea2/peinarse.why: The gloss is right. The affirmative imperatives read peínate, peínese, peínense, the add_stress fault: the stress falls on the e of the diphthong, péinate. The first example, 'Sabe cómo tiene que peinarse el cabello', is not natural Spanish.
dropEx: Sabe cómo tiene que peinarse el cabello.
ex: Me peino todas las mañanas.
I comb my hair every morning.

delea2/cansarse.why: The gloss is right. The first example, 'men tire themselves in pursuit of rest', is an aphorism, and the third was sexual. The second's English said 'store'.
dropEx: Los hombres se cansan en búsqueda del descanso.
Solíamos hacer el amor
exEn: Ya me canso de andar por la tienda
I'm getting tired of walking round the shop.
ex: Me canso mucho cuando subo escaleras.
I get very tired when I climb stairs.
Los niños nunca se cansan de jugar.
Children never get tired of playing.

delea2/preferir.why: 'to rather' is not English. The second example, 'Preferiría que te quedes', breaks the sequence of tenses (quedaras).
dropEx: Preferiría que te quedes
ex: ¿Prefieres té o café?
Would you rather have tea or coffee?

delea2/cepillarse.why: The gloss is right. The third example, 'Come antes de cepillarse los dientes', is not a sentence anyone needs.
dropEx: Come antes de cepillarse los dientes.
ex: Me cepillo los dientes tres veces al día.
I brush my teeth three times a day.

delea2/chatear.why: The card had two examples, and the second, a man called César plugging in an extension lead to chat in bed, is not a sentence anyone needs.
dropEx: César conectó el alargador
ex: Paso horas chateando con mis amigos.
I spend hours chatting with my friends online.
¿Chateamos luego?
Shall we chat later?

delea2/soler.why: The gloss was a trailing definition. The first example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A1: the A1 card, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: to usually do, to tend to (suelo + infinitive — I usually …)
dropEx: Los lobos no suelen atacar a la gente.
ex: Suelo levantarme a las siete.
I usually get up at seven.

delea2/apellidarse.why: The card had two examples. The first's English said 'Bro' for tío, and both said 'last name' for the British 'surname'.
senses: to have the surname (me apellido García — my surname is García)
exEn: cómo dijiste que te apellidabas
Mate, what did you say your surname was?
Sabes cómo se apellida
Do you know his surname?
ex: Me llamo Ana y me apellido García.
My name is Ana and my surname is García.

deleb1/hacerse.why: The gloss and the examples are right. The gerund read hacíendose, S3's reflexive-gerund fault, and is now haciéndose. The first example's English said 'a member in this library'.
exEn: hacerse miembro de esta biblioteca
It's very easy to become a member of this library.

deleb1/gracias.why: The gloss did not give dar las gracias. The first example is also an A1 sentence, and the second was gracias a, 'thanks to', which is its own card later in B1 and which lost its meaning in the English ('The storm knocked out power'). SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Daniel les dio las gracias a los policías.
gracias a la tormenta
ex: Muchas gracias por venir.
Thank you very much for coming.
Dale las gracias a tu madre de mi parte.
Thank your mother for me.

deleb1/el hecho.why: NONE OF THE THREE EXAMPLES WAS THE NOUN. Each was the participle hecho, hecha, 'made', of hacer, A1's card: 'la tarta que ha hecho ella', 'hechas de vidrio', 'hecha de plástico'. De hecho, 'in fact', is its own card later in B1.
senses: el hecho de que — the fact that
dropEx: la tarta que ha hecho ella
están hechas de vidrio
está hecha de plástico
ex: El hecho es que no tengo tiempo.
The fact is that I don't have time.
No me gusta el hecho de que llegues tarde.
I don't like the fact that you're late.
La policía investiga los hechos.
The police are investigating what happened.

deleb1/el tipo.why: The gloss missed tipo meaning a man, 'bloke', which every Spaniard uses, and ran the two rates in without their nouns. The first example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: rate (tipo de cambio — exchange rate; tipo de interés — interest rate)
dropEx: el tipo de cambio de hoy
ex: Es un tipo muy simpático.
He's a really nice bloke.

deleb1/la parte.why: The gloss did not give the phrases this word lives in. The first example is shared with la mochila in A2, and the third with así in A2. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: la mayor parte de — most of
dropEx: Se me olvidó mi mochila en alguna parte.
no irás a ninguna parte mañana
ex: La mayor parte de mis amigos viven aquí.
Most of my friends live here.
—¿De parte de quién? —De Ana.
'Who's calling?' 'Ana.'

deleb1/la idea.why: The gloss is right. The second and third examples were one construction, ideas different from someone else's, and the third is shared with diferente in A2. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: no tengo ni idea — I've no idea
dropEx: Tu idea es completamente diferente de la mía.
ex: No tengo ni idea de dónde está.
I've no idea where it is.

deleb1/el amor.why: The gloss is right. The first example, '¡Por amor de Cristo!', is an oath rather than a sentence a learner needs.
dropEx: Por amor de Cristo
ex: Se casaron por amor.
They married for love.

deleb1/buenas.why: NONE OF THE THREE EXAMPLES WAS THE GREETING. Each was the adjective buenas, the plural of bueno, A1's card: 'buenas intenciones', 'buenas notas', 'cosas buenas'; and the second is also an A1 sentence.
senses: hello, hi (informal, at any time of day)
dropEx: tiene buenas intenciones
Para tener buenas notas
merece cosas buenas
ex: ¡Buenas! ¿Qué tal estás?
Hi! How are you?
Buenas, ¿tienen pan de centeno?
Hello, have you got rye bread?
¡Buenas a todos!
Hello, everyone!

deleb1/la forma.why: The gloss did not give estar en forma, 'to be fit'. The second example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: estar en forma — to be fit
dropEx: La lengua se puede usar de diferentes formas.
ex: Hago deporte para estar en forma.
I do sport to keep fit.

deleb1/el camino.why: NONE OF THE THREE EXAMPLES COULD STAY. The first is shared with medio in A2, the second with cualquiera in A2, and the third, a flowery path to glory, is an aphorism shared with conducir in A1. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: No te des por vencido a medio camino.
tomar cualquiera de los dos caminos
Ningún camino de flores
ex: ¿Sabes el camino a la estación?
Do you know the way to the station?
Nos perdimos por el camino.
We got lost on the way.
Voy de camino a casa.
I'm on my way home.

deleb1/la ayuda.why: NONE OF THE THREE EXAMPLES COULD STAY. The first two were the verb ayudar, A1's card ('ayuda a cualquiera', 'si tú nos ayudas'), and the third is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: ayuda a cualquiera que se lo pida
si tú nos ayudas
contar con la ayuda de otros
ex: Te agradezco mucho la ayuda.
I'm very grateful for the help.
¿Necesitas ayuda con las maletas?
Do you need help with your suitcases?
¡Ayuda! ¡Me ahogo!
Help! I'm drowning!

deleb1/siquiera.why: The gloss put 'at least' first; at B1 the word is ni siquiera, 'not even', which every example is. The third, 'Ni siquiera la ciencia es una ciencia exacta', is an aphorism.
dropEx: Ni siquiera la ciencia
ex: Se fue sin siquiera decir adiós.
He left without even saying goodbye.

deleb1/feliz.why: 'merry (trait)' is not a sense. The first and third examples were one construction, the happiest something in the world.
dropEx: Es el lugar más feliz en la tierra
ex: ¡Feliz cumpleaños, Ana!
Happy birthday, Ana!

deleb1/la muerte.why: 'the personification of death as a hooded figure' is not a sense a learner needs. The first and third examples were one construction, a count of deaths.
dropEx: El número de muertes resulta impactante.
ex: Su muerte fue una sorpresa para todos.
His death came as a surprise to everyone.

deleb1/la realidad.why: 'commodity' is not this word. The first and third examples were one construction, a dream coming true; the first, once the name table ran, is also A2's el sueño sentence, and the third is shared with finalmente in A2. En realidad is its own card later in B1. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Su sueño se ha convertido finalmente en realidad.
El sueño de Carlos se está haciendo realidad.
ex: La realidad es muy distinta.
The reality is very different.
A veces la realidad supera a la ficción.
Sometimes truth is stranger than fiction.

deleb1/a menudo.why: 'oftentimes' is American. The second example used enojar, which is Latin American; Spain says enfadar. The first, once the name table ran, is also A2's el dolor sentence. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: hace enojar a la gente a menudo
Carlos sufre a menudo de dolores de cabeza.
ex: Vamos a menudo a la playa.
We often go to the beach.
Nos vemos a menudo.
We see each other often.

deleb1/el corazón.why: The gloss is right. The first example's English, 'I'm out of breath', is not what 'se me sale el corazón por la boca' means, and the third, a proverb, is shared with sentir in A1. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Se me sale el corazón por la boca.
Ojos que no ven
ex: Tiene un corazón de oro.
She has a heart of gold.
El corazón late más rápido cuando corres.
Your heart beats faster when you run.

deleb1/suficiente.why: The gloss is right. The third example, 'A veces el amor simplemente no es suficiente', has no full stop and is shared with a veces later in B1; both cards now lose it. SHARED WITHIN B1: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
dropEx: A veces el amor simplemente no es suficiente
ex: No hay suficiente comida para todos.
There isn't enough food for everyone.

deleb1/el equipo.why: The gloss put 'hardware' among the senses and did not show equipment, which none of the examples used. The first example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Su equipo es más fuerte que el nuestro.
ex: ¿Dónde has dejado el equipo de esquí?
Where have you left the ski kit?

deleb1/el doctor, la doctora.why: The gloss put 'Ph.D.' first; at B1 the word is a doctor you visit. The first example's English said 'office hours'.
exEn: tiene el doctor la consulta
What are the doctor's surgery hours?

deleb1/la sangre.why: The gloss is right. The first example, '5 puntos de sangre', is a video game's hit points.
dropEx: solo le quedan 5 puntos de sangre
ex: Me sale sangre de la nariz.
My nose is bleeding.

deleb1/darse.why: The gloss had come apart ('to give oneself • darse cuenta • to realize'). The first example is shared with medio in A2, and the second read 'lo que estaba pasado' for pasando. The usted imperative read dése, which since the 2010 spelling rules is written dese.
senses: darse por vencido — to give up
darse un golpe — to bump, to hit oneself
dropEx: No te des por vencido a medio camino.
lo que estaba pasado
ex: Me di cuenta de lo que estaba pasando.
I realised what was happening.
Se dio un golpe en la cabeza.
He hit his head.

deleb1/el sentido.why: The gloss gave 'way (manner)' and missed meaning and direction. The third example, 'un completo y total sin sentido', is not Spanish (S16 dropped the same sentence from completar in A2).
senses: meaning (no tiene sentido — it makes no sense)
dropEx: completo y total sin sentido
ex: Tiene un gran sentido del humor.
She has a great sense of humour.

deleb1/a veces.why: The gloss is right. The first example is also an A1 sentence, the second is shared with el sentido earlier in B1, and the third, with no full stop, with suficiente. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1). SHARED WITHIN B1: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
dropEx: A veces el mundo parece no tener sentido.
A veces el amor simplemente no es suficiente
Todo el mundo quiere a alguien a veces.
ex: A veces voy al trabajo en bici.
Sometimes I cycle to work.
A veces llueve mucho en abril.
Sometimes it rains a lot in April.
Mi hermano me ayuda a veces.
My brother helps me sometimes.

deleb1/la palabra.why: 'wording' is not a separate sense. The second example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: le gustan los juegos de palabras
ex: ¿Qué significa esta palabra?
What does this word mean?

deleb1/matar.why: The gloss put 'slay' among the senses. The second example was the noun las mates, 'maths', not the verb, and the first, a proverb, is shared with morir in A2. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: El que a hierro mata
no le gustan las mates
ex: El gato mató un ratón.
The cat killed a mouse.
El accidente mató a dos personas.
The accident killed two people.

deleb1/el sitio.why: The gloss missed room, space, which is what ¿hay sitio? asks. The first example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: room, space (¿hay sitio? — is there room?)
dropEx: Ella se fue a comprar a otro sitio.
ex: ¿Hay sitio para uno más?
Is there room for one more?

deleb1/así que.why: The gloss is right. The first example is shared with así in A2, and the third with el hambre in A2. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: no irás a ninguna parte mañana
Acabo de comer, así que no tengo hambre.
ex: Llovía, así que nos quedamos en casa.
It was raining, so we stayed at home.
Es tarde, así que me voy a dormir.
It's late, so I'm going to bed.

deleb1/el dado.why: The first and third examples were one sentence, Einstein's line about God and dice, twice.
dropEx: ¡Dios no juega a los dados!
ex: Te toca tirar los dados.
It's your turn to throw the dice.

deleb1/el paso.why: The second and third examples were the verb pasar ('Pasa por mí', 'si pasas por la tienda'), not the noun, and the third is also an A1 sentence. The gloss missed the zebra crossing.
dropEx: Pasa por mí a las dos y media.
si pasas por la tienda
ex: Dio un paso hacia la puerta.
He took a step towards the door.
Oí pasos en la escalera.
I heard footsteps on the stairs.

deleb1/la falta.why: The gloss missed hacer falta, 'to be needed', and a foul in sport. The first example is also an A1 sentence, and the third was the verb faltar ('le falta confianza') and is an A1 sentence too. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: hacer falta — to be needed (no hace falta — there's no need)
dropEx: Las flores mueren con la falta de agua.
A Carlos le falta confianza
exEn: tus faltas de asistencia
You must account for your absences.
ex: No hace falta que vengas.
You don't need to come.
El árbitro pitó falta.
The referee blew for a foul.

deleb1/otra vez.why: The gloss opened on Wiktionary's own note ('Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see otra, vez'). The first example is shared with junto in A2, and the second with la respuesta in A2. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: volver a cantar juntos alguna otra vez
Inténtalo otra vez
ex: ¿Otra vez llegas tarde?
Are you late again?
Lo intentaré otra vez mañana.
I'll try again tomorrow.

deleb1/perdido, perdida.why: The gloss is right. The first example was the verb perder in a perfect tense ('hemos perdido un tiempo'), not the adjective, and the third's English said 'lost and found'.
dropEx: Ya hemos perdido un tiempo más que suficiente.
exEn: objetos perdidos más cercana
Where is the nearest lost property office?
ex: Estoy perdido, ¿me puedes ayudar?
I'm lost, can you help me?

deleb1/llevarse.why: The gloss put the phrase llevarse bien without its adverb. The second example is also an A1 sentence, and the first and third were one construction, getting on with someone; the first's English said 'get along'. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: to take (away), to take with you
llevarse bien / mal con — to get on well / badly with
dropEx: se llevó algo de comida a casa
no se lleva bien con sus vecinos
exEn: no puede llevarse bien con Ana
Carlos just can't get on with Ana.
ex: ¿Te llevas el paraguas?
Are you taking your umbrella?
Los ladrones se llevaron el coche.
The thieves took the car.

deleb1/real.why: The gloss missed 'royal', which the third example is.

deleb1/la orden.why: The first example was el orden, 'order, sequence', a different word of the other gender, and the third spelt the plural's accent onto the singular, órden. The gloss's 'order (request, purchase, or food)' is Latin American; Spain says pedido.

The captain gave the order to attack.
La policía tenía una orden de registro.
The police had a search warrant.

deleb1/especial.why: The gloss said 'special' twice, and missed 'particular, fussy', which the first example is. The third is shared with la educación in A2. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: una clase de educación especial
ex: Hoy es un día muy especial.
Today is a very special day.

deleb1/duro, dura.why: The gloss missed hard as difficult. The second example was the verb durar, A2's card ('nada dura para siempre'), not the adjective.
dropEx: A fin de cuentas, nada dura para siempre.
ex: Ha sido un día muy duro.
It's been a very hard day.

deleb1/el puesto.why: NONE OF THE THREE EXAMPLES COULD STAY. The first is shared with junto in A2, the second with nuevo in A1, and the third was the participle puesta of poner ('llevas puesta la chaqueta'), not the noun. The gloss missed the market stall. cuarenta nuevos puestos de trabajo
llevas puesta la chaqueta

The team finished in third place.

deleb1/al menos.why: The gloss is right. The first example, 'al menos que le hablen', is a mistake for a menos que, 'unless', which is its own card later in B1; it and the third are also A1 sentences. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).

vi al menos cincuenta películas
ex: Llámame al menos una vez a la semana.
