Al menos no llueve.
At least it isn't raining.

deleb1/extraño, extraña.why: The gloss was a list of eleven synonyms and missed the noun, a stranger, which the second example is.

deleb1/raro, rara.why: The gloss put 'rare' first; at B1 raro is strange or weird, which two examples are. The third is shared with sacar in A2. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: has sacado esos zapatos
ex: Es raro que no haya llamado.
It's odd that she hasn't called.

deleb1/general.why: The gloss did not give por lo general, which the first and third examples both were, or the noun, a general. The third also carried a Freddy the name table does not reach.
dropEx: mis amigos me llaman Freddy
ex: El director general llega mañana.
The managing director arrives tomorrow.

deleb1/el modo.why: The gloss put 'mood' beside 'way' without saying it is the grammar term, and missed de todos modos. The third example is also an A1 sentence. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Ahora veo la vida de un modo diferente.
ex: No hay modo de convencerlo.
There's no way to convince him.

deleb1/asesino, asesina.why: THE CARD HAD NO EXAMPLES, and glossed only the adjective, 'murderous', where the word is overwhelmingly the noun, a murderer.
senses: el asesino, la asesina — murderer, killer
ex: La policía detuvo al asesino.
The police arrested the murderer.
El asesino huyó por la ventana.
The killer escaped through the window.
Es una novela sobre una asesina.
It's a novel about a woman who kills.

deleb1/encontrado, encontrada.why: 'facing, opposite' is not what the adjective means now; it is sentimientos encontrados, 'mixed feelings'. The three examples were one construction, something being found.
dropEx: La piedra Rosetta fue encontrada en 1799.
ex: Tengo sentimientos encontrados sobre este viaje.
I have mixed feelings about this trip.

deleb1/el control.why: The gloss was a definition. The first example is also an A1 sentence, and the third, 'se fue fuera de su control', is not natural Spanish. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).

dropEx: Conforme pasa el tiempo
ex: No estoy conforme con la decisión.
I'm not happy with the decision.

deleb1/la cesta.why: The gloss is right. All three examples were a basket full of something.
dropEx: Ella tenía una cesta llena de manzanas
ex: Echa la ropa sucia en la cesta.
Put the dirty clothes in the basket.

deleb1/adoptar.why: The gloss carried a stray 'N' line and said 'to adopt' twice. The first and third examples were both adopting an idea or a method.
dropEx: Me gustó tu idea y la
ex: Adoptamos un perro de la protectora.
We adopted a dog from the animal shelter.

deleb1/el músculo.why: The gloss said 'muscle tissue, muscle (organ)'. The card had two examples, and the first is shared with el acero earlier in B1. SHARED WITHIN B1: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
dropEx: Sus músculos estaban duros como el acero.
ex: Hay que estirar los músculos antes de correr.
You should stretch your muscles before running.
El corazón es un músculo.
The heart is a muscle.

deleb1/la contabilidad.why: The gloss gave 'accountancy' only, where the examples are bookkeeping and the accounts department.

deleb1/el pintado.why: THE WRONG WORD, WITH NO EXAMPLES. The card was glossed 'the tattooed indigenous people of Cebu during the Spanish occupation of the Philippines' — a historical ethnonym no B1 syllabus asks for — and carried none. The word a B1 learner needs is the participle-adjective pintado, 'painted', as in recién pintado, 'wet paint'. This is a judgement: the source list gives the bare form, and the generator chose the noun. Renamed and given three examples.
ex: Cuidado, recién pintado.
Careful, wet paint.
Tenía las uñas pintadas de rojo.
She had her nails painted red.
La puerta está pintada de verde.
The door is painted green.

deleb1/la ficha.why: The card had one example, 'No debería haber saltado la ficha', an idiom its English rendered 'blown a fuse', and the gloss gave 'chip, token' without a form or a counter in a game.
dropEx: haber saltado la ficha
ex: Mueve tu ficha.
Move your piece.
Rellene esta ficha con sus datos.
Fill in this form with your details.
Cada jugador empieza con diez fichas.
Each player starts with ten counters.

deleb1/gobernar.why: The gloss is right. The first example was the noun gobierno and is shared with el gobierno in A2, and the third said the queen reigns in England, which stopped being true in 2022. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: La culpa de todo la tiene el gobierno
la reina reina pero no
ex: El partido gobierna desde hace cuatro años.
The party has been in government for four years.
Es difícil gobernar sin mayoría.
It's hard to govern without a majority.

deleb1/laboral.why: The gloss said 'labor', American. The examples are right.

deleb1/católico, católica.why: The gloss gave 'well (feeling well)' without the phrase it comes from. The first two examples' English wrote catholic in lower case.
senses: no estar muy católico — to feel a bit off-colour
exEn: Ser católico no te hace
Being Catholic doesn't make you better than me.
pero no va a la iglesia
She's Catholic, but doesn't go to church.

deleb1/la extensión.why: The gloss put 'tract (an area)' first. The second example was urban-planning jargon about kerb extensions and the third a sentence about the separation of powers.
dropEx: extensiones del bordillo
El poder judicial no debería
ex: Llámame a la extensión 214.
Call me on extension 214.
España tiene una extensión de medio millón de kilómetros cuadrados.
Spain covers about half a million square kilometres.

deleb1/la fibra.why: The gloss gave 'fibre' twice in two spellings. The third example's English said 'bran'.
exEn: No te olvides de tomar mucha
Remember to eat lots of fibre.

deleb1/el sustituto, la sustituta.why: The gloss is right. The first example is not a natural sentence, and the third spelt the word substituto, a variant the card does not teach.
dropEx: El nuevo hogar funciona
Soy profesor substituto
ex: Vino un profesor sustituto.
A supply teacher came.
La miel es un buen sustituto del azúcar.
Honey is a good substitute for sugar.

deleb1/reclamar.why: The gloss put 'to reclaim, to recover possession of' first and did not give 'to complain'. The second example's English said 'I'll take what's mine'.
exEn: lo que me pertenece
I'll claim what belongs to me.

deleb1/blando, blanda.why: The gloss gave 'bland', a false friend (soso). The third example was a medical symptom.
dropEx: Tengo heces blandas
ex: Este colchón es demasiado blando.
This mattress is too soft.

deleb1/la calefacción.why: The gloss is right. The third example's English said 'dorm'.
exEn: de nuestro dormitorio no está
The heating in our bedroom isn't working properly.

deleb1/la mostaza.why: The gloss is right. The third example said giraffes are mustard-coloured.
dropEx: Las jirafas son color
ex: ¿Quieres mostaza en el perrito caliente?
Do you want mustard on your hot dog?

deleb1/la pulsera.why: The gloss is right. The first and third examples were both reloj de pulsera, and the second, 'Women often use bracelets', is a generalisation with the wrong verb.
dropEx: Tu reloj de pulsera está
Las mujeres usan frecuentemente
ex: Le regalé una pulsera de plata.
I gave her a silver bracelet.
Lleva una pulsera en cada muñeca.
She wears a bracelet on each wrist.

deleb1/el cocodrilo, la cocodrila.why: The gloss is right. The second example, crocodiles never eating chocolate, is not a sentence a learner needs.
dropEx: nunca comen chocolate
ex: Vimos cocodrilos en el río.
We saw crocodiles in the river.

deleb1/el pescador, la pescadora.why: The gloss was a definition. The examples are right.

deleb1/el psicólogo, la psicóloga.why: The gloss is right. The second and third examples were about Pepperberg's parrot research and Koko the gorilla, which a learner has no way to place.
dropEx: la investigación de Pepperberg
el CI de Koko
ex: Mi hermana es psicóloga infantil.
My sister is a child psychologist.
El psicólogo me ayudó mucho.
The psychologist helped me a lot.

deleb1/el tenedor.why: The gloss is right. The second and third examples both asked for knives and forks.
dropEx: Danos dos cuchillos y cuatro
ex: Se come la pasta con tenedor.
You eat pasta with a fork.

deleb1/dividir.why: The gloss is right. The first two examples both divided food into three, and the first used torta, Latin American for tarta.
dropEx: dividió la torta
ex: El río divide la ciudad en dos.
The river divides the city in two.

deleb1/el/la protagonista.why: The gloss gave 'star' without saying it means the lead in a film. The first and third examples were the same question about a protagonist's fate.
dropEx: qué pasa al final con el
ex: Ella es la protagonista de la obra.
She plays the lead in the play.

deleb1/el funcionario, la funcionaria.why: The gloss did not give 'civil servant', which is what the word usually means. The card had two examples, and the first sneered at the speaker's mother for doing nothing.
dropEx: mi madre tampoco hacía nada
ex: Mi madre trabaja de funcionaria en el ayuntamiento.
My mother works for the town council.
Los funcionarios hacen huelga hoy.
Civil servants are on strike today.

deleb1/medir.why: The gloss did not give medir for height, which the first and third examples are. The second example is a stiff passive, and the third's English spelt 'meter'.
dropEx: Me gustaría ser medido
exEn: Los dos medimos
We're the same height. We're both 1.70 m tall.
ex: Mide la mesa antes de comprar el mantel.
Measure the table before you buy the tablecloth.

deleb1/la provincia.why: The gloss is right. The first example, a cloud of smoke over the province, has no context, and the second's English gave 'the Rio Plata'.
dropEx: Hay una nube de humo
exEn: Provincias Unidas del Río
In 1816, the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata declared their independence from Spain.
ex: España tiene cincuenta provincias.
Spain has fifty provinces.

deleb1/el gorro.why: The gloss did not give estar hasta el gorro, which the second example is. The third's English said 'tuque'.
senses: estar hasta el gorro — to be fed up
exEn: Ella perdió su
She lost her hat, but found it later.

deleb1/moreno, morena.why: The gloss was American and did not give 'tanned', the everyday sense in Spain. The first example's English said 'black' hair, and the second, about liking brunettes, is not a sentence a learner needs.
dropEx: A Carlos le gustan las morenas
exEn: El pelo de ese chico es
That boy's hair is dark.
ex: Volvió muy morena de la playa.
She came back very tanned from the beach.

deleb1/afectar.why: ALL THREE EXAMPLES WENT. The first is shared with nacional earlier in B1 and the second with enseguida in A2; the third was the noun afecto. The gloss carried a stray 'N' line and 'to feign'. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1). SHARED WITHIN B1: the earlier card keeps the sentence.
dropEx: La huelga ha afectado
les afecta enseguida el frío
vínculo de afecto
ex: La noticia le afectó mucho.
The news affected him deeply.
La sequía afecta a toda la región.
The drought is affecting the whole region.
El tabaco afecta a la salud.
Tobacco affects your health.

deleb1/apartado, apartada.why: The gloss gave 'different'. The second example's English rendered apartada as 'reserved'.
dropEx: Estaba incómoda y apartada
ex: Viven en un pueblo muy apartado.
They live in a very remote village.

deleb1/cuadrado, cuadrada.why: The gloss is right. The first example was the noun el cuadrado.
dropEx: Un cuadrado tiene cuatro lados
ex: La habitación mide doce metros cuadrados.
The room is twelve square metres.

deleb1/el congelador.why: The gloss is right. The first and third examples were one sentence, and the second described finding a dead baby in a freezer.
dropEx: el cuerpo de un recién nacido
se comió todo el helado
ex: Mete la carne en el congelador.
Put the meat in the freezer.
El congelador está lleno.
The freezer is full.

deleb1/el atentado.why: The gloss was a list. The card had two examples, and the second dated an era by '9.11'.
dropEx: Desde el 9.11
ex: Hubo un atentado en el centro de la ciudad.
There was an attack in the city centre.
La policía evitó un atentado.
The police prevented an attack.

deleb1/artístico, artística.why: The gloss is right. The third example, calling the wish to survive and the fear of death 'artistic sentiments', is nonsense.
dropEx: son sentimientos artísticos
ex: Tiene mucho talento artístico.
She has a lot of artistic talent.

deleb1/coser.why: The first two examples were the noun cosa, 'thing', and the second is shared with otro in A1. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
dropEx: Tómate las cosas un poco
no hace otra cosa sino leer
ex: Mi abuela me enseñó a coser.
My grandmother taught me to sew.
¿Me puedes coser este botón?
Can you sew this button on for me?

deleb1/ingresar.why: The gloss gave only joining and enrolling. The first example is paying money in; the second's ingresaron al ejército should be en el; the third was the noun ingreso. Being admitted to hospital was missing.
dropEx: ingresaron al ejército
en función del ingreso
exEn: 100 dólares en su cuenta
He paid 100 dollars into his savings account.
ex: Lo ingresaron en el hospital.
He was admitted to hospital.
Ingresó en la universidad a los dieciocho años.
She went to university at eighteen.

deleb1/individual.why: The gloss gave 'case-by-case' and not 'single', as in una habitación individual. The third example's estilo propio individual is redundant.
dropEx: un estilo propio individual
ex: Pedimos una habitación individual.
We asked for a single room.

deleb1/el triángulo.why: The gloss gave 'control arm', a car part. The first and third examples were the same definition.
dropEx: Si una figura tiene tres lados
ex: Dibuja un triángulo en la pizarra.
Draw a triangle on the board.

deleb1/el titular.why: The gloss carried a stray 'N' line and did not give el/la titular, a holder. The third example was the verb titularse.
senses: el/la titular — holder (of an account, a post)
dropEx: Cómo se titula este libro
ex: El accidente salió en los titulares de todos los periódicos.
The accident made the headlines in every paper.

deleb1/plantar.why: The gloss carried a stray 'N' line and did not give dejar plantado. The first two examples were the noun planta, shared with después and la planta in A1. SHARED WITH A LOWER DECK: the lower deck, which a reader meets first, keeps the sentence and this card is given a fresh one (see batch S1).
senses: dejar plantado a alguien — to stand someone up
dropEx: Las plantas crecen rápidamente
sobre esta extraña planta
ex: Plantamos tomates en el huerto.
We planted tomatoes in the vegetable garden.
Me han dejado plantado.
I've been stood up.

deleb1/crudo, cruda.why: The gloss was a list, 'rare, underdone' among it. The examples are right.

deleb1/la decoración.why: The gloss is right. The first and third examples ('La decoración no es mala', 'Me encanta la decoración') say nearly nothing.
dropEx: Me encanta la decoración
ex: Ella se encargó de la decoración del salón.
She took care of decorating the living room.

deleb1/mareado, mareada.why: The gloss was a list of five. The first example was the verb marearse in the perfect.
senses: sick (in a car, on a boat)
dropEx: Te has mareado alguna vez
ex: Estaba mareado después del viaje en autobús.
He felt sick after the bus journey.

deleb1/solicitar.why: The gloss put 'to solicit, to attract' in a list and not 'to apply for', which the first example is. The second's audiencia is a calque (el público), and the third was a job advert asking for women only.
dropEx: entre la audiencia
específicamente a una dama
ex: Solicité una beca para estudiar en Francia.
I applied for a grant to study in France.
Puede solicitar más información en recepción.
You can ask for more information at reception.

delea1.why: THE DECK HAD NO THIRD-PERSON OBJECT PRONOUN AT ALL. supplement.py's PRONOUNS list names me, te, se, nos and os and stops, so DELE A1 shipped with cards for los and unas and nothing for lo, la, le or les - the pronouns an A1 reader needs the moment they stop using a noun twice in a sentence. The only trace of them was the los card's gloss, which called it 'a plural masculine or neuter pronoun' and gave no English at all; that card is now folded into the definite article, so without this the sense would have gone entirely. It also carries the neuter article lo, which turns an adjective into a noun (lo importante) and is a construction with no other home in the deck. The paradigm goes in Forms rather than in the headword, so the front of the card is not one letter away from the article's. Its Forms rows are the pronoun's own paradigm and not words to mark up, so the card names what may be bolded: deriving from them would bold the ARTICLE la in 'lo importante es la salud'.
senses: the … thing, what is … (neuter, before an adjective: lo importante)
ex: No lo sé.
I don't know.
Lo compré ayer.
I bought it yesterday.
Lo importante es la salud.
The important thing is health.

delea1.why: The indirect object, missing for the same reason as lo. It carries the se rule in Forms - le and les become se before lo, la, los and las - which is the one thing about Spanish pronouns a reader cannot guess, and which the deck already shows in an example on the por card ('¿Por qué no se lo dijiste a ella?') without ever explaining. les is a form rather than a card, on the same reasoning that folded el, la, los and las into one.
senses: to him, to her, to you (formal) — indirect object
ex: Le di el libro a María.
I gave the book to María.
¿Qué le pasa?
What's the matter with him?
Les escribí una carta.
I wrote them a letter.

delea1.why: cómo had a card and como, one accent away and just as common, had none - so the deck taught the question word and not the ordinary conjunction that means 'as' or 'like'. It is also the one that turns up in a comparison (tan alto como) and in a reason clause (como llueve, no salgo), neither of which the deck could say anywhere. It is also the first person of comer, which is why the comer card's own examples bold it.
forms: with an accent, the question word
ex: Es tan alto como su padre.
He's as tall as his father.
Trabaja como profesor.
He works as a teacher.
Como llueve, no salgo.
Since it's raining, I'm not going out.

delea1.why: esto and eso each had a card and aquello, the third of the same set of three, had none - so the deck taught two thirds of a closed class and left the reader to guess the rest.
senses: that (neuter, further off — an idea, a situation, or something not yet named)
ex: Aquello fue muy difícil.
That was very difficult.
No me gustó nada aquello.
I didn't like that at all.
¿Te acuerdas de aquello?
Do you remember that?

delea1.why: The same gap as como, one accent over. supplement.py's QUESTION list names the ACCENTED interrogatives - qué, quién, cómo, cuándo, dónde, cuánto - and the deck therefore taught six question words and not one of the ordinary conjunctions written the same way without the accent. cuando is among the commonest words in Spanish and had no card. (donde is added beside it; quien and cual are deliberately left out — the relative quien is a B1 word and el cual is further on still, so adding them here would be teaching above the level rather than filling a gap.)
forms: with an accent, the question word
ex: Te llamo cuando llegue.
I'll call you when I arrive.
Cuando era niño, vivía en Madrid.
When I was a child, I lived in Madrid.
Ven cuando quieras.
Come whenever you like.

delea1.why: See the cuando entry: the unaccented half of a question word the deck taught only as a question.
senses: where (as a relative: la casa donde vivo — the house where I live)
forms: with an accent, the question word
ex: Esta es la casa donde vivo.
This is the house where I live.
Vamos donde tú quieras.
Let's go wherever you like.
El pueblo donde nació es muy pequeño.
The village where he was born is very small.
